title: Ethiopian Chicken with Lentils
community: All of Ethiopia — the combined protein family dish
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Doro Misir — chicken simmered in a berbere sauce with red lentils added in the final 25 minutes. The lentils dissolve into the chicken sauce, thickening it naturally and adding plant protein. The complete family meal — chicken and lentil together.
longDesc: Doro Misir is the practical family wat — chicken extended with red lentils produces a dish that is simultaneously more nutritious and more economical than pure chicken wat. The lentils absorb the berbere and create a thick, complete sauce.
steps: Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Add chicken. Coat in sauce.
Lentils should dissolve and thicken the sauce.
chefTips: Add lentils after the chicken is half-cooked.
Red lentils dissolve — they thicken the sauce naturally.
commonMistakes: Adding lentils too early — they disintegrate before chicken is cooked.
cookingScience: See ETH057 for chicken-and-lentil cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Lentils extend chicken further — more sustainable protein combination.
healthBenefits: Complete protein from chicken and lentils together.
culturalNote: Doro Misir is the Ethiopian cook's smart answer to feeding a large family well — the combination of chicken and lentils produces more than the sum of their parts, both nutritionally and in flavour.
